_comment: Minimum tests that must EXECUTE per project. The control for defect class DC-012: a crashed test host reports success with a smaller count, and nothing else notices. Raise these with `python tools/verify-test-run.py --update` when you add tests; never lower one to make a run pass. Keys with a suffix are HALVES of a project run on one OS; `splits` says which halves must account for which whole, and verify-test-run checks that sum on every invocation, on both operating systems. AiDe.Core.Tests.nonportable is [Trait("Platform","Windows")] only - kernel32, powershell.exe, the net10.0-windows daemon, and tests that assert Windows path semantics on purpose. There is no quarantine category: every test that merely failed on Linux was diagnosed and fixed (INV-0005).
_baselineBump: 2026-09-11, merge of node F6 (feature/provider-config) — the providers.json reader and the composer handshake. App 512 -> 517; Core 2210 -> 2234, portable 2056 -> 2080, non-portable unchanged at 154. MEASURED on the merged tree, each key its own run: --filter Platform!=Windows gave 2080, --filter Platform=Windows gave 154, the whole Core run gave 2234, and 2080 + 154 = 2234 by OBSERVATION. The first App run on this tree reported NO RESULTS and the second reported one failure; neither was the product. The first was contention with a backgrounded gate loop of my own that held the DLLs, and the second was a STALE out-of-process probe (DC-023, fourth instance) — AiDe.App.ComposerProbe was not a ProjectReference, so the test ran a binary built 32 minutes before the fixes it asserts. Both are recorded because a floor set from a run I did not understand is a guess with a number on it. verify-test-run.py --update was NEVER run and no node edited this file — baselines are the conductor's separate recorded act, because a node raising its own floor is grading its own work. Every floor raised; none lowered. Prior bumps: F4b App 504 -> 512; C2 + corpus-assertion App 495 -> 504, Core 2206 -> 2210, portable 2052 -> 2056.
